documents.abstract: In contemporary higher technical education, academic institutions affiliated with large engineering universities face significant hurdles in monitoring student learning trajectories, diagnosing root conceptual deficiencies, and providing timely faculty interventions. Traditional examination systems rely predominantly on post-hoc summative grade sheets that report aggregate percentages without uncovering why a student struggles. Furthermore, standard Learning Management Systems (LMS) and black-box predictive models provide ungrounded score predictions, lack pedagogical explainability, suffer from generative AI hallucinations, and neglect strict multi-tenant institutional privacy boundaries. To overcome these fundamental challenges, this paper presents EDU-VISION, an end-to-end, explainable academic intelligence and diagnostic learning gap framework designed for engineering curricula. EDU-VISION integrates a domain-constrained Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline, deterministic student performance profiling, an explainable non-judgmental learner classification model, a prioritized six-category diagnostic learning gap detection engine, and an assignment-scoped faculty intervention lifecycle. By grounding exam generation and evaluation in verified university marking schemes, the system eliminates metric fabrication. Furthermore, deterministic algorithms classify learner progression across four evidence-backed tiers, diagnose specific cognitive gaps (Concept, Answer Writing, Scheme Alignment, Application, Revision, and Consistency), and recommend verified pedagogical resources. Faculty members receive assignment-scoped intelligence dashboards with non-causal longitudinal tracking, protected by enterprise-grade distributed rate limiting and multi-college boundary isolation. Keywords— Educational Intelligence, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Learning Gap Detection, Explainable AI, Faculty Intervention, Academic Analytics, Multi-Tenant Architecture.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: This paper examines how artificial intelligence-mediated and human translation practices co-construct gendered meaning within digital environments. Approaching translation as an active reconfiguration of linguistic and multimodal cues, the study contrasts the tendency of computational systems to reproduce normative gender binaries with the human capacity to negotiate contextual nuance. Through an empirical analysis of English-to-Romanian translations in the beauty sector, the research exposes the ethical and cognitive implications of automated workflows, particularly the amplification of embedded cultural biases. Integrating sociocultural semiotics and algorithmic auditing, the paper proposes a collaborative model of translation. This framework leverages the efficiency of neural machine translation while relying on practitioner reflexivity to mitigate systemic distortions. Ultimately, human expertise remains an essential mechanism for guiding automated systems toward culturally responsible representations of identity in automated translational landscape.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinated whole-body interaction with the physical world, yet collecting robot demonstrations at scale remains costly. Human demonstrations offer a scalable alternative, but existing egocentric human supervision often omits locomotion and posture, while embodiment differences and controller dynamics hinder accurate end-effector execution. We introduce HumanVerse, a 500-hour dataset of open-world human loco-manipulation pairing egocentric video with synchronized body and hand motion. Our human-to-humanoid pipeline aligns camera viewpoints and arm appearance, and refines motion references and controller inputs offline to reduce end-effector errors while preserving whole-body coordination. We validate the pipeline through zero-shot transfer to Unitree G1 on representative whole-body manipulation and long-range loco-manipulation tasks, without target-task robot demonstrations. Building on this pipeline, we develop $λ_0$, a humanoid foundation model for whole-body loco-manipulation, with robot-aligned human demonstrations providing supervision for mid-training. Increasing whole-body human data consistently improves downstream task progress. $λ_0$ achieves 90.0% success on SIMPLE and 62.5% across real-world loco-manipulation tasks. We expect this study to guide scalable whole-body human data collection toward humanoid foundation models for richer interaction with the physical world. Homepage: https://lambdahumanoid.github.io/

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as judges to predict which of two candidate answers a human evaluator would prefer, providing a scalable alternative when human evaluation is too costly. Unfortunately, LLM judgments can exhibit systematic biases. Prior work has documented position, verbosity or model family of the candidate answers influencing the judge decision rather than their quality, while additional biases may remain undocumented. $\textit{Multicalibration}$ provides a natural framework to address this problem: each bias corresponds to miscalibration on an identifiable group, $\textit{e.g.}$, family bias manifests as overconfidence in answers generated by models belonging to the same family of the judge. The challenge is to fix miscalibration simultaneously across many, potentially unknown groups. To this end, we introduce $\mathrm{CaLLM}$, a post hoc framework that multicalibrates an LLM judge, thereby bounding all such biases simultaneously. We prove that $\mathrm{CaLLM}$ bounds the bias of every group whose error structure is captured by an available representation, and that augmenting it with explicit bias groups further reduces the residual bias. We then derive theoretical conditions under which $\mathrm{CaLLM}$ improves the judge's accuracy, rather than trading it for calibration. Finally, we evaluate $\mathrm{CaLLM}$ across pairwise preference benchmarks, showing that it reduces the multicalibration error on both specified and unspecified bias groups, while improving predictive performance of the judge.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Nigeria’s power grid experiences recurring partial and total collapses that cause widespread electricity outages and socioeconomic disruption. This study proposes a cloud-based system that combines grid-collapse prediction with coordinated disaster-recovery management. The predictive component uses a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network–Long Short-Term Memory model. The CNN identifies local patterns within multivariate grid data, while the LSTM captures temporal relationships that may indicate developing instability. Disaster recovery is organised through a three-horizon “Now, Next, and Later” framework. “Now” focuses on immediate stabilisation, situational awareness, communication, incident coordination, and restoration of critical loads. “Next” covers staged restoration, cause assessment, resource deployment, and a return to stable operation. “Later” addresses predictive maintenance, infrastructure reinforcement, preventive investment, model improvement, and organisational learning. It is designed to complement rather than replace existing protection and control-room systems. The framework was evaluated using simulated Nigerian power grid data. The CNN-LSTM achieved 95.5% accuracy, 96.0% precision, 95.0% recall, an F1-score of 95.0%, and an ROC-AUC of 0.982. Median inference latency was 184 milliseconds, and the false-alarm rate was 2.4%. The recovery module correctly classified 98.6% of 500 simulated actions into Now, Next, and Later. A regional service-failure exercise restored essential service in 7 minutes 42 seconds with a 46-second recovery point. These results show that the prototype provides a scalable, economically viable solution to enhance grid resilience in developing power systems with limited resources and infrastructure constraints. The framework also shows how artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and structured disaster-recovery planning can be integrated into a unified decision-support approach for improving Nigerian grid resilience.

Abstract Agriculture is a major component of many countries’ economies worldwide, especially in developing nations. The major challenge farmers face is the rapid spread of plant diseases, which often goes unnoticed and causes major yield and economic losses. Traditional methods such as human inspection and laboratory testing are often time-consuming, inaccurate, labor-intensive, and unsuitable for large-scale farming. To overcome these challenges, advanced technologies like Machine learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) have emerged in recent times, providing early and accurate detection of plant diseases. This paper focuses on recent advances in applying deep learning techniques, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), to detect plant diseases. Across 1081 publications from 2014 to 2024, studies show that CNNs are well suited to extracting and analyzing features from plant images and clearly distinguishing healthy from diseased specimens. The models discussed in the surveyed literature generally report performance in terms of key parameters such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, which this review compiles and discusses rather than benchmarking through new experiments. The results show high accuracy and strong potential for real-world agricultural applications. The bibliometric analysis reveals growing interest and collaborative efforts in the research domain, especially among institutions specializing in artificial intelligence and agriculture. Moreover, the results support the practical application of deep learning in agriculture for plant health monitoring and highlight the importance of comprehensive studies in solving agricultural problems. The study provides a foundation for further innovations in automated plant disease detection and supports the transition to smart farming solutions.

Microalgae are third generation feedstock and an alternative for the development of biodiesel through sustainable application which are environment friendly. This paper delves in utilization of microalgae for biodiesel and other value-added products. The microalgae cultivation procedure can become cost effective by utilizing wastewater from domestic and industrial origin for the purpose of biomass and subsequent lipid production. This paper addresses all the breakthrough of microalgae in biotechnological applications and also how machine learning and artificial intelligence can be applied to make the process more favourable and technoeconomic analysis of harvesting and other process has also been discussed. The growth of microalgae and different methods and equipment to achieve high amount of biomass is explored efficiently. This paper emphasizes the use of heterogenous catalyst instead of homogenous because of its reusability and the easy availability of precursors and calcium oxide sources in the environmental wastes like oyster shells, egg shells and waste animal bones. Overall, this chapter delves into the advantages and challenges of utilizing microalgae for the process of biodiesel production and provides alternative methods to address and minimize those challenges for sustainable and economically feasible procedures.

Large Language Model-guided Evolutionary Search (LLM-ES), exemplified by AlphaEvolve, has recently demonstrated impressive performance in solving goal-driven problems with extremely large and complex search spaces. Unlike conventional LLM approaches based on single-shot or few-shot sampling, LLM-ES introduces population-based evolution to iteratively generate more novel and higher-quality solutions. Compared with traditional Evolutionary Computing algorithms, LLM-ES treats LLMs as semantic variation operators. This design extends the search space from low-dimensional vectors to expressive and language-defined structures such as code and programs. Meanwhile, the rich prior knowledge embedded in LLMs significantly improves the efficiency of evolutionary search in complex solution spaces. As a result, LLM-ES effectively exploits the test-time scaling capability of LLMs and achieves state-of-the-art performance in many open-ended problems. In this survey, we provide a systematic overview of this emerging field. We first formalize the problem setting and the general pipeline of LLM-ES. We then review existing works from several key perspectives, including population design, prompt builder, LLM model selection, evaluation design, and exploration-exploitation control. Finally, we summarize representative applications and discuss open challenges and future research directions.

The rapid growth of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionised numerous facets of human life, particularly for Generation Z, who have been raised in a predominantly digital milieu. Adolescents are progressively impacted by AI (AI) technology in the realms of knowledge construction, decision-making, and learning. Although AI presents several prospects for creativity, education, and productivity, it raises ethical concerns around autonomy, critical thinking, authenticity, responsibility, and human dignity. This conceptual paper examines ethical considerations regarding the employment of AI among Generation Z through Immanuel Kant's philosophical framework. It is recently being enhanced by the viewpoint of Magnifica Humanitas, which underscores the dignity, greatness, and flourishing of the human individual. This article deeply examines Kantian concepts like good will, autonomy, obligation, illumination, the categorical imperative, and the premise of humanity as a goal in itself, which accomplished through a philosophical-conceptual methodology. This study posits that AI is not merely a technological innovation; but rather a social force that impacts human behaviour and cognition. Kantians contend that ethical interaction with AI is not chiefly contingent upon technological progress, instead it hinges on humans' capacity to uphold rational autonomy and moral accountability in their dealings with intelligent systems. The essay contends that educational institutions possess a moral obligation to enhance Generation Z's knowledge of AI by instructing them to utilise AI deliberately and ethically, rather than dissuading their engagement. In additon, Magnifica Humanitas views AI must serve as an instrument for human advancement and should never replace morality, rationality, or human dignity. The research concludes that, in a progressively automated society maintaining humanity's status as the paramount moral being is crucial for the ethical implementation of AI.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: The African mining industry continues to face a serious communication gap between technical safety documentation and the language used by the workforce. Safety manuals, operating procedures, and regulatory guidance are often produced in English or French, while many workers communicate in isiZulu, chiShona, and other local languages. This mismatch is not just inconvenient; it can be dangerous in safety-critical settings where misunderstandings may contribute to preventable incidents. This paper reports on Talk MINING, a domain-adapted multilingual large language model built on InkubaLM and trained on mining-specific text, question–answer pairs, and multimodal hazard data. The model was developed using Hugging Face tools and evaluated with both quantitative and qualitative methods. Results show a marked improvement over the baseline model, with overall accuracy rising from below 50% to 82%, and strong gains across isiZulu, chiShona, and English. The project also includes a web-based prototype that allows users to take photos of mining conditions and receive guidance in a local language. This paper presents the full pipeline for Talk MINING, including document preparation, translation and localization, model training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and validation. Beyond benchmark performance, the system is designed for practical deployment in environments where connectivity is limited and literacy levels vary—supporting both text queries and image-based hazard input through a mobile-ready prototype. The work contributes a reproducible pipeline, a curated multilingual mining corpus, and an open evaluation framework that can serve as a foundation for extending domain-adapted AI to other African languages and safety-critical industries. Ultimately, Talk MINING demonstrates that closing the language gap in mining safety is not only technically feasible but achievable with relatively modest model size when domain adaptation is done rigorously.

Large language models (LLMs) increasingly act as personal assistants; however, little is known about how they capture national-level preferences on a global scale. Given that "time" is a universal and representative concept, we examine LLMs' time preferences by varying only users' country and measuring the compensation LLMs deem appropriate for a 60-minute appointment delay. We then compare LLMs' responses with GDP per capita on Purchasing Power Parity (GDP_PPP), Mean Income, and a literature-based index (Patience Score). Our results across 193 countries and 5 LLMs demonstrate that people's time across the world is evaluated in noticeably different ways among LLMs, as well as varying levels of robustness under prompt variations. LLMs consistently recommend the highest compensation for Europe, but mostly the lowest for Africa. Based on GDP_PPP, LLMs underestimate the value of time for users living in Asia and South America. These findings indicate that geographical patterns are embedded in LLMs and may translate in different treatment in agentic settings.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Data augmentation (DA) is a critical technique for addressing data sparsity. Existing DA methods suffer from several limitations: extensive parameter tuning, dependency on specific types of data, and the tightly coupled DA network in the backbone recommendation model. Consequently, there remains a notable absence of universal data augmentation frameworks capable of adapting to diverse recommendation tasks and backbone models. To address these issues, we propose a hybrid framework to mitigate data sparsity via DA in a more flexible and universal paradigm. Notably, we disentangle the data augmentation process into two modules, data generation and data fusion. Firstly, we prompt LLMs to learn collaborative filtering information from raw user–item interaction data in a CSV format, generating new reliable interactions. Specifically, we devise clustering-based data grouping and multi-round shuffling strategies to enable LLMs to capture comprehensive collaborative filtering information through limited context. Secondly, we design an adaptive sampler to obtain personalized fused data for backbone recommendation models dynamically, making the fused data satisfy the different data demands of diverse downstream recommendation models. Experiments on various recommendation models across distinct datasets demonstrate that our framework can consistently improve vanilla recommendation models and facilitate existing DA methods. Compared with vanilla recommendation models, our framework achieves an average performance gain of 7.10%, 23.54%, and 24.55% on MovieLens-100k, Book-Crossing, and Toys and Games datasets, respectively. These results highlight the effectiveness of our proposed framework in mitigating data sparsity in recommender systems.

A IMPORTÂNCIA DA PRÁTICA DA GINÁSTICA LABORAL PARA OS PROFISSIONAIS DA EDUCAÇÃO RESUMO Este artigo trata-se de um recorte da Dissertação de Mestrado que aborda sobre a importância da prática da ginástica laboral como intervenção de atividade física para a melhoria da saúde e da qualidade de vida desses docentes. A rotina dos profissionais da educação é marcada por intensa carga de trabalho, longos períodos em pé ou sentados e movimentos repetitivos, fatores que contribuem para o surgimento de Distúrbios Osteomusculares Relacionados ao Trabalho (DORT). O objetivo geral do trabalho é identificar os impactos biopsicossociais da aplicação de programas de ginástica laboral no ambiente escolar. A metodologia consistiu em uma revisão bibliográfica de caráter qualitativo, utilizando bases de dados eletrônicas como SciELO, Google Acadêmico e Lilacs. Os resultados indicam que a ginástica laboral atua significativamente na redução do estresse, no alívio de dores musculares crônicas e na prevenção de lesões por esforço repetitivo. Além disso, a prática promove a socialização e melhora o clima organizacional nas instituições de ensino. Conclui-se que a inserção da ginástica laboral na rotina escolar constitui uma estratégia preventiva indispensável, necessitando de maior apoio de políticas públicas e da gestão escolar para sua real consolidação e continuidade. Palavras-chave: Ginástica Laboral. Profissionais da Educação. Saúde do Trabalhador. THE IMPORTANCE OF WORKPLACE GYMNASTICS PRACTICE FOR EDUCATION PROFESSIONALS ABSTRACT The routine of education professionals is marked by intense workload, long periods standing or sitting, and repetitive movements, factors that contribute to the emergence of Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders (WMSD). This article analyzes the importance of workplace gymnastics as a physical activity intervention to improve the health and quality of life of these teachers. The general objective is to identify the biopsychosocial impacts of implementing workplace gymnastics programs in the school environment. The methodology consisted of a qualitative literature review using electronic databases such as SciELO, Google Scholar, and Lilacs. The results indicate that workplace gymnastics acts significantly in reducing stress, relieving chronic muscle pain, and preventing repetitive strain injuries. Furthermore, the practice promotes socialization and improves the organizational climate in educational institutions. It is concluded that the insertion of workplace gymnastics into the school routine constitutes an indispensable preventive strategy, requiring greater support from public policies and school management for its actual consolidation and continuity. Keywords: Workplace Gymnastics. Education Professionals. Occupational Health. LA IMPORTANCIA DE LA PRÁCTICA DE LA GIMNASIA LABORAL PARA LOS PROFESIONALES DE LA EDUCACIÓN RESUMEN Este artículo es un extracto de una tesis de maestría que aborda la importancia de la gimnasia en el lugar de trabajo como intervención de actividad física para mejorar la salud y la calidad de vida del profesorado. La rutina de los profesionales de la educación se caracteriza por cargas de trabajo intensas, largos periodos de pie o sentados y movimientos repetitivos, factores que contribuyen a la aparición de trastornos musculoesqueléticos relacionados con el trabajo (TMERT). El objetivo general de este trabajo es identificar los impactos biopsicosociales de la aplicación de programas de gimnasia en el lugar de trabajo en el entorno escolar. La metodología consistió en una revisión cualitativa de la literatura utilizando bases de datos electrónicas como SciELO, Google Scholar y Lilacs. Los resultados indican que la gimnasia en el lugar de trabajo reduce significativamente el estrés, alivia el dolor muscular crónico y previene lesiones por esfuerzo repetitivo. Además, la práctica promueve la socialización y mejora el clima organizacional en las instituciones educativas. Se concluye que la inclusión de la gimnasia en el lugar de trabajo en la rutina escolar constituye una estrategia preventiva indispensable, que requiere un mayor apoyo de las políticas públicas y la administración escolar para su consolidación y continuidad. Palabras clave: Gimnasia en el lugar de trabajo. Profesionales de la educación. Salud del trabajador.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Abstract This study develops a monotone pairwise redundancy-aware Artificial Age Score (AAS) for event-level decision burden in human–robot collaboration (HRC). Six normalized inputs describe safety and operational burden, with illustrative weights and conceptual overlaps. Logarithmic evidence is aggregated with a symmetric pairwise discount. Sufficient conditions guarantee coordinatewise monotonicity, additive contributions provide computational traceability, and an independent gate preserves detected mandatory-review conditions. On 13,762 held-out non-mandatory Sobol profiles, the method yielded a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC) of 0.892 (95% bootstrap interval 0.887-−0.897) and balanced accuracy of 0.800 (0.793-−0.806) against a synthetic oversight policy, versus 0.880 and 0.788 for redundancy-free AAS 0 . Pairwise AAS produced no decreases in 1,179,648 coordinatewise checks, versus 3,484 for the ratio comparator. Measurement-error tests used 300 noise runs and 54 signed-offset settings without threshold retuning. In all 15 noise conditions, pairwise AAS retained higher mean score-only balanced accuracy, whereas AAS 0 had higher mean gate-plus-score balanced accuracy. Under an all-input $$-0.05$$ offset, pairwise rank correlation remained 0.9896, but 20.97% of score decisions changed and 5.19% of clean mandatory profiles were missed. Thus, rank stability and non-override do not ensure decision stability or correct sensing. The findings establish mathematical properties and synthetic behavior, not empirical calibration, field effectiveness, or operator understanding. Real HRC and human-factors validation remain necessary.

EarthTrends is a multi-source Earth Observation framework developed to assess the impact of permafrost thaw on land degradation across the Arctic. Rapid warming is accelerating processes such as thermokarst formation, vegetation change, slope instability, and risks to infrastructure, yet monitoring these dynamics requires integrating heterogeneous satellite datasets and analytical methods. EarthTrends addresses this challenge through a modular Python architecture that fuses long-term satellite archives (Landsat), Copernicus Sentinel data, MODIS time series, and high-resolution optical imagery with advanced statistical and artificial intelligence approaches. The framework quantifies ecosystem change using multi-sensor vegetation index time series analysed through linear regression, Mann–Kendall trend tests, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models to detect non-linear dynamics and anomalies. Thermokarst features are automatically mapped from high-resolution imagery using a U-Net deep learning segmentation model. Land degradation susceptibility is further evaluated by modelling soil freeze–thaw cycles as proxies for slope instability and landslide potential. Environmental indicators are intersected with socio-economic datasets to estimate impacts on settlements and infrastructure. Preliminary results show that the thermokarst detection component is operational and capable of identifying surface subsidence features, while freeze–thaw analyses reveal anomalies linked to areas of increased degradation risk. Vegetation trends highlight spatially heterogeneous ecosystem responses to warming across the Arctic. Overall, EarthTrends demonstrates the feasibility of an integrated, scalable framework for monitoring permafrost-driven environmental change and its societal implications. The system is intended for pan-Arctic application and will be released as an open-source tool to support research, monitoring, and decision-making related to climate-induced land degradation.

Background The United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) catalogs in vitro diagnostics, including Nucleic Acid Amplification Tests (NAATs), using unstructured clinical terminology. Because these regulatory labels often diverge from standardized biological taxonomy, they obstruct automated post-market surveillance and computational integration, particularly for in silico inclusivity audits against emerging pathogen variants. This study aimed to build a reproducible computational pipeline that translates historical FDA microbial NAAT records into machine-actionable biological identifiers. Methods Synthesizing clinical diagnostic logic, taxonomic normalization rules, and modern text mining, the workflow utilized the R ellmer package to interface with a Large Language Model (LLM) for Technology Classification, successfully isolating true NAATs from 510(k) summary documents. Subsequent algorithmic partitioning and LLM-driven Named Entity Recognition (NER) mapped complex syndromic labels and clinical abbreviations to National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) Taxonomy Identifiers (TaxIDs). Results While only 20% of initial FDA records mapped directly to NCBI Taxonomy, the automated deconvolution of syndromic panels and NER extraction expanded and normalized the dataset. The pipeline successfully generated FDA510kPathogens, a highly granular master repository containing 457 unique pathogen-to-submission entries formally linked to enriched NCBI TaxIDs and metadata. Conclusions By programmatically translating human-readable regulatory metadata into machine-actionable biological descriptors, this open-source digital infrastructure resolves a critical informatics bottleneck. This provides diagnostic laboratories and developers with the foundational data necessary to conduct continuous, automated validation of molecular assays.

Background: Workplace stress, anxiety, burnout and psychological distress are important concerns affecting employee well-being and organisational performance. The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in digital mental health support offers opportunities for accessible and timely assistance, while raising concerns regarding privacy, informed consent, algorithmic bias, clinical safety, accountability and human oversight. This study aims to examine the potential role and responsible integration of AI-based psychiatric counselling for managing employee stress and supporting workplace mental health by 2030. Materials and Methods: A mixed-methods research design will be used, combining quantitative survey data with qualitative interviews. The quantitative component will include approximately 350–450 employees, while the qualitative component will involve approximately 25–35 interviews with HR professionals, organisational leaders, EAP professionals and mental health practitioners. Data will assess perceived stress, anxiety, burnout, psychological safety, trust, confidentiality, privacy concerns, AI counselling acceptance and willingness to use AI-based mental health support. Quantitative data will be analysed using descriptive statistics, reliability testing, correlation, regression, t-tests, ANOVA and appropriate mediation or moderation analyses. Qualitative data will be analysed thematically. Results: The study is expected to identify factors influencing employee acceptance and trust in AI-based psychiatric counselling and to examine the role of privacy, human oversight, psychological safety and organisational support in its responsible adoption. Conclusion: AI-based psychiatric counselling may serve as a supportive component of workplace mental health systems, particularly for early support, psychoeducation, self-help and triage. However, it should complement rather than replace qualified mental health professionals. Responsible implementation will require privacy safeguards, informed consent, clinical oversight, transparency, fairness, accountability and clear referral pathways.

Despite their importance for maintaining infrastructure integrity, manual culvert inspections pose significant operational challenges for agencies such as the Utah Department of Transportation (UDOT) due to high labor demands, subjective assessments, and variability in evaluation outcomes. This study investigates the application of computer vision for automated culvert inspection, leveraging both supervised machine learning and emerging vision–language models. We proposed a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)–enhanced multimodal large language model (MLLM) framework that interprets culvert-condition imagery based on the culvert inspection manual. By embedding a small set of curated visual exemplars into a shared space, we enabled image-based retrieval to ground model reasoning alongside the full inspection manual. For the MLLM component, we selected three open-source models (Qwen3-VL, Gemma-3, LLaVA-OneVision) and one proprietary model (Gemini-3-Flash). We evaluated performance using precision, recall, and F1-score, alongside a practical “most-severe-label” decision rule to simulate maintenance prioritization. Results showed that the RAG-enhanced Gemini-3-Flash achieved the highest severity accuracy (91.16%), outperforming the supervised ConvNeXt multi-label baseline (84.54%) and other evaluated MLLMs. Overall, the findings suggest that RAG-enhanced Gemini-3-Flash can improve the reliability of severity-relevant decisions while reducing data-labeling requirements by approximately 99% (from thousands of training images to just 127 exemplars) and the GPU-intensive training burden, with the primary trade-offs being reliance on proprietary APIs and token-based inference costs.
topics: Industrial Vision Systems and Defect Detection

documents.abstract: This theoretical discussion paper examines how artificial intelligence participates in cognition, judgment, and generative activity through historically constituted relations among models, humans, other artificial agents, institutions, and environments. It distinguishes equal access to foundational technical capability from equality of situated performance, evaluative and generative judgment, practical opportunity, social recognition, and authority. A preliminary Generative Relational Theory (GRT) perspective treats historically conditioned AI configurations as candidates for relational reality where sufficiently stable causal efficacy can be established, while suspending claims about consciousness and ultimate ontological status. The analysis considers how interaction histories, conversational practices, memory, feedback, aesthetic preferences, and normative criteria may shape the realization of AI capabilities. It also investigates coordination conventions and rule-like practices among interacting AI agents, their uncertain normative authority, and the distinct processes through which generated contributions acquire recognition and institutional influence. Findings from existing experiments and field studies are interpreted within their task-specific limits, including evidence concerning heterogeneous productivity, creative diversity, contextual accommodation, and collective coordination. A comparative research program is proposed to distinguish historical causal contributions from prompt effects, unequal information, institutional selection, and other rival explanations. Relational differentiation may coexist with convergence or the reduction of existing disadvantages. The paper neither reports new experiments nor establishes a general law of AI-mediated inequality; questions of legitimacy and justice require normative arguments in addition to causal analysis.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Vaccines are administered to large populations of healthy individuals, including vulnerable groups, making an exceptionally rigorous safety profile a prerequisite for their approval and use. Nonclinical vaccine safety assessment has traditionally relied on standardized animal testing methodologies, which face increasing challenges: the ethical imperative to reduce animal use, the need for faster vaccine development, and the limitations of animal models in predicting human-specific immune responses. The advent of modern vaccine platforms such as mRNA technologies and viral-vector vaccines necessitates a re-evaluation of safety frameworks. This article explores emerging strat­egies to modernize vaccine safety assessment, integrating new approach methodologies (NAMs), including in vitro systems, artificial intelligence, and adverse outcome pathways (AOPs). Ethical refinements to animal husbandry practices, including group housing, humane endpoints, pain man­agement and scaled blood sampling volumes, are also discussed to align with the principles of the 3Rs (replacement, reduction, refinement). The adoption of molecular and omics-based techniques, along with innovative validation strategies, offers opportunities to improve predictive accuracy and mechanistic insight. The article highlights a strategic framework for implementing NAMs across the three stages at which animals are still used – early screening, late nonclinical development, and batch release – while ensuring alignment with regulatory requirements. Implementation must be careful enough to ensure that the use of NAMs in the safety evaluation of vaccines maintains or exceeds current safety assessment standards. By addressing scientific, ethical, and regulatory challenges, NAMs have the potential to transform vaccine safety assessment, enhancing human relevance and accelerating innovation in vaccine development. Plain language summaryThis article examines the evolving landscape of vaccine safety assessment, focusing on opportunities to modernize testing approaches through new approach methodologies (NAMs). Drawing on recent discussions with stakeholders across industry, academia, and regulatory bodies, we outline key chal­lenges and strategic pathways for implementing NAMs in vaccine development while maintaining robust safety standards. Special attention is given to emerging technologies, such as human-relevant test systems, artificial intelligence, and virtual control groups, to the replacement of animal-based potency, pyrogen and adventitious agent tests used for batch release, and to considerations for regu­latory acceptance and implementation strategies.

topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: Abstract Background In natural language processing, word sense disambiguation (WSD) is still a significant difficulty, especially in low-resource, multilingual environments with few annotated resources. Contextual semantic representation and WSD performance have been enhanced by recent developments in transformer architectures and large language models (LLMs). However, there is still little evidence synthesis in multilingual and genuine low-resource situations, and research is still dispersed across architectures, datasets, and evaluation systems. Methods In order to map evidence on transformer and LLM-based Word Sense Disambiguation techniques published between 2019 and January 2026, this scoping study used the PRISMA-ScR methodology. Google Scholar database was searched for relevant literatures. Studies that used transformer or LLM-based techniques for WSD and reported evaluation criteria like accuracy or F1-score were considered eligible. A structured framework comprising model architectures, datasets, evaluation techniques, adaption strategies, and important discoveries was used to chart the data descriptively. Results Nine studies were included in the analysis. Gloss-aware transformers, poly-encoder architectures, multilingual transfer learning, morphologically aware fine-tuning, parameter-efficient adapters, and LLM-based reasoning were among the main topics. Model scale alone does not seem to have as much of an impact on WSD performance as architectural design and contextual modeling. Evidence for really low-resource languages was still scarce, though. Conclusion Transformer and LLM-based methods show immense potential for improving WSD in multilingual contexts. However, there are still gaps in robustness assessment, benchmark standardization, and the wider inclusion of low-resource languages that are underrepresented.

This study develops an evidence-based, context-sensitive framework for inclusive elevator system design in China. Drawing on the Capability Approach, the Biopsychosocial Model, inclusive design perspectives, and social ecology, it combines qualitative interviews and quantitative surveys to examine users’ capabilities, psychological processes, and social interactions across age groups and elevator contexts. The findings indicate that elevator experiences reflect interactions among physical and cognitive capabilities, psychological perceptions, and socially shared behaviors. Older adults showed greater mobility and sensory constraints, middle-aged users reported stronger hygiene and emergency-related concerns, and younger users showed greater sensitivity to efficiency and interpersonal pressure. Differences were also identified between residential and public elevators. The Function–Behavior–Structure framework was then used to translate these behavioral findings into prioritized design recommendations. The proposed approach supports targeted responses where user needs differ while maintaining standardized solutions for shared social norms, providing a transferable pathway for inclusive public infrastructure design.
topics: Assistive Technology in Communication and Mobility

documents.abstract: Machine learning systems that make automated decisions, including fraud flags, loan denials, and safety interlocks, typically generate an explanation (for example via SHAP) in the same trust domain as the model itself, leaving no independent proof that the explanation shown to an auditor is the one the model actually produced at decision time. This research presents and empirically evaluates a blockchain-anchored explainable-AI (XAI) audit-trail architecture that closes this gap by committing a canonical SHA-256 hash of each decision-and-explanation record to an Ethereum-compatible ledger, while keeping the full record, including the SHAP explanation, off-chain. The architecture is implemented end to end on a real fraud-detection pipeline consisting of a LightGBM classifier trained on the IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection dataset (590,540 transactions), a SHAP TreeExplainer layer producing per-transaction feature attributions, a canonical JSON serialization and hashing procedure, and two complementary Solidity smart contracts: one committing each audit record individually, and the other committing batches of records via a Merkle root. Using 500 audit records, the schemes are benchmarked on an Ethereum-compatible network across batch sizes of 10 to 500 records and extended with synthetic hashes to 1,000, 2,500, and 5,000 records. Individual commitment registers a record in 6.3 to 17.4 ms at 139,300 gas per record. Merkle-root batching reduces on-chain gas consumption by 91.6% at 10 records to 99.98% at 5,000 records, with reduction factors rising from roughly 12-fold to nearly 5,982-fold. Tamper-detection trials correctly flagged altered records in 100% of cases. The work contributes a reproducible, empirically costed reference architecture for verifiable AI explanation integrity, and a direct, quantified comparison of two on-chain commitment strategies across three orders of magnitude of batch size that prior blockchain-XAI proposals have not benchmarked head to head.
topics: Blockchain Technology in Education and Learning

documents.abstract: Uzbek and Mandarin Chinese lie at opposite ends of the morphological spectrum: Uzbek is an agglutinative Turkic language with SOV order and a rich case system, whereas Chinese is an isolating Sino-Tibetan language with SVO order, function words and numeral classifiers, written without word boundaries. Our search did not identify a systematic, openly available Uzbek–Chinese parallel corpus; the only directly relevant study found builds a filtered, partly LLM-generated pseudo-parallel dataset from news crawls. This paper proposes a typology-informed methodological model for building such a corpus. It has five components: (1) a layered design separating a human-verified gold core, an automatic extension and a labelled synthetic layer, with provenance metadata; (2) asymmetric linguistic processing linked through Universal Dependencies; (3) multi-level alignment down to the morpheme, with correspondence-type labels; (4) a "unit–set of equivalents" lexical database; and (5) retrieval-augmented integration with large language models. A correspondence table and two author-composed sentence pairs show that most grammatical correspondences are not one-to-one. An evaluation protocol is specified for future empirical work.

This thesis examines the psychological nature, components, and causes of academic burnout among students. Academic burnout is interpreted as a consequence of an imbalance between academic demands and personal resources. The factors that play an important role in its prevention, including self-regulation, self-efficacy, social support, intrinsic motivation, and teacher–student relationships, are analyzed. Furthermore, the main directions of psychological and pedagogical prevention are systematized.

Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is reshaping academic practice in higher education, yet evidence on how students evaluate its acceptable uses remains limited. This study surveyed 988 post-secondary students across 39 countries, recruited through the Prolific online research platform, on the acceptability of GenAI use across 22 academic tasks using a binary Yes/No format. Using an interpretive framework grounded in normative boundary-setting, academic integrity values, and academic socialization, the analysis reveals differentiated acceptability patterns: Students endorse GenAI for instrumental and research-support tasks while maintaining normative boundaries around evaluative and judgement-intensive activities. Gender differences are minimal; level of study is the primary source of variation, with graduate students reporting higher acceptability for research- and professionally oriented uses. Respondents residing in Canada (n = 58) reported significantly lower acceptance of four text-focused tasks, including academic composition and summarization, than the non-Canadian cohort. Findings have implications for institutional policy, pedagogy, and academic integrity frameworks.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: The rapid proliferation of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) and Digital Learning Resources (DLRs) has fundamentally transformed the pedagogical landscape globally. However, for students with disabilities in Indian school settings, digital transformation presents a dual reality of unprecedented educational opportunity and severe systemic exclusion. This doctoral study investigates the physical, pedagogical, and technological accessibility of digital learning platforms and evaluates their empirical effectiveness on learning outcomes, cognitive engagement, and social inclusion for students with diverse disabilities across primary and secondary schools in India.Employing a mixed-methods sequential explanatory research design (N=450), data were systematically collected across urban, semi-urban, and rural school establishments in West Bengal, Maharashtra, and the National Capital Region (NCR). Quantitative assessments involved Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2.1 AA) technical compliance audits of flagship state and national digital portals (including DIKSHA, PM e-VIDYA, and SWAYAM Prabha) alongside standardized Likert-scale surveys measuring technological self-efficacy, user satisfaction, and learning gains.

Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training improves robot foundation models (RFMs) beyond their demonstrations, but real-world deployment demands more: learning new tasks efficiently while retaining previously acquired behaviors. Existing continual RL methods on top of VLAs mitigate forgetting but rely on on-policy updates with limited forward transfer, whereas off-policy methods improve single-task sample efficiency without addressing learner persistence across tasks. We propose ACCRUE, a continual off-policy RL framework that carries lightweight actor and critic networks across tasks, allowing each stage to reuse behavioral and value knowledge acquired through prior RL. The inherited critic adapts only on current-task transitions and guides current-task actor learning, while prior behavior is preserved by distilling the actor toward cached targets on a small number of retained episodes. Fixed visual features keep the inherited learner and its replay compatible with base-policy updates. Across contact-rich assembly sequences in simulation and on real-robot hardware, ACCRUE accelerates subsequent-task learning with near-zero forgetting and significantly reduces real-robot training time by 31.0\% to 68.5\%.

World Action Models (WAMs) use generative visual representations to condition robot actions, yet how these representations organize action-relevant information remains poorly understood. We identify persistent high-norm spatial outliers in WAM representations and find that their action relevance persists even after normalization and K/V projection attenuate their extreme magnitude. Motivated by this observation, we introduce RegisterWAM, which adds learnable non-spatial registers to the world model and uses them directly for action conditioning. Registers alone do not fully eliminate spatial outliers; pairing them with observation flow-matching (FM) loss supervision suppresses spatial outliers while concentrating high-norm responses in registers. Beyond this reorganization, observation FM loss supervision also improves action learning without registers, motivating an additional noised-observation FM objective that learns current-scene recovery from corrupted inputs. The resulting model achieves 81.64\% success on LIBERO-Plus without additional embodied pretraining data or foundation models, reaches 93.0\% average success on RoboTwin 2.0, and improves real-world manipulation performance.

This paper examines acupressure and occupational health promotion through a structured academic review of contemporary literature. The discussion considers the conceptual background of acupressure, research findings, possible explanatory mechanisms, methodological quality, practical applications, safety, and future research needs. Acupressure has been investigated in relation to several patient-reported and functional outcomes, although findings vary across populations and intervention protocols. Differences in point selection, pressure technique, session duration, comparator groups, sample sizes, and outcome instruments make direct comparison difficult. The paper therefore emphasizes cautious interpretation and evidence-based integration. Particular attention is given to the distinction between complementary use and replacement of conventional care.

Autoimmune pancreatitis (AIP) is an immune-mediated inflammatory condition of the pancreas that can be difficult to differentiate from pancreatic malignancy and therefore remains challenging to diagnose. Type 1 AIP is the pancreatic manifestation of immunoglobulin G subclass 4-related disease and can be associated with other systemic fibro-inflammatory conditions. Type 2 AIP is characterised histologically by granulocytic epithelial lesions and is frequently associated with inflammatory bowel disease. Over the previous years, endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) has become an important part of the diagnostic work-up of patients presenting with suspected AIP, particularly when imaging studies demonstrate focal pancreatic enlargement, or a mass-like lesion. Recent advances in EUS imaging, including contrast-enhanced harmonic EUS and EUS elastography, may improve characterisation of the pancreatic lesion and help distinguish an inflammatory pancreatic process from a pancreatic malignancy. Moreover, EUS-guided tissue acquisition plays an important role in this context by allowing histological assessment of the lesion and hence helping exclude a malignancy. EUS-guided fine-needle biopsy is currently the preferred tissue acquisition technique, as it allows the preservation of tissue architecture, which helps facilitate the diagnosis of AIP. A multidisciplinary approach involving a panel of specialists in hepatopancreatobiliary endoscopy, hepatology, rheumatology, radiology, cardiology, nephrology, and histopathology is valuable for integrating the different components of the diagnostic work-up and guiding subsequent management. Finally, emerging artificial intelligence algorithms for EUS may support the diagnostic process and facilitate recognition of AIP. This review discusses current and emerging EUS techniques, tissue acquisition options, safety considerations, multidisciplinary integration and the potential role of artificial intelligence in the diagnosis and management of AIP.

Modern pipelines integrating multi-omics data, chemical libraries, structural biology information and artificial intelligence are currently accelerating drug discovery and precision medicine. Aligned with these advances, the multi-omics profiling technologies enable the identification of unique genetic and epigenetic signatures for stratification of patients based on cancer specific target and vulnerability. Targeted therapies to specific receptor or enzyme mutated or overexpressed often fail because cancer cells can adapt quickly. Tumor cells overgrow driven by new gene mutation and parallel crosstalk of signaling pathways. Patients with cancer and the hereditary syndrome targets such as BRCA1/2, and emerging targets such as ATR, CHK1, WEE1, and POLθ, are hypersensitive to ionizing radiation and PARP inhibitors. Combining synthetic lethality inhibitors, chemotherapy and immunotherapy effectively kill cancer cells by breaking multiple survival signaling pathways. Antibodies to immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting molecules like PD-1, PD-L1, and CTLA-4 can improve survival of patients, though predictive immunotype remains challenging. Emerging pharmacological approaches combining either epigenetic modifiers, oncomicrobiotics or engineered bacteria sequentially convert tumors into a highly antigenic, T cell-inflamed, and checkpoint-responsive tumor, providing a mechanistically grounded framework for next-generation precision immunotherapy. However, large human clinical trials remain necessary to standardize protocols, biomarkers and long-term efficacy. Cancer vaccines have evolved through rational engineering synthetic mRNA encoding tumor-specific antigens or tumor-associated antigens. This will enable the next generation of truly therapeutic and preventive vaccines for many cancers. This review provides a timely synthesis of the basic mechanisms for rational multidrug treatments for cancers.

ABSTRACT Air pollution from sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ) emissions poses significant threats to environmental sustainability, public health, and climate change efforts. Despite advances in monitoring and regulatory frameworks, traditional methods often fall short in accuracy, scalability, and efficiency. This study explores the transformative potential of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in environmental monitoring, SO 2 emission prediction, and desulfurization. It utilizes a literature review of research from 2013 to 2025, assessing AI and ML models for air pollution monitoring, SO 2 emission forecasting, catalytic desulfurization, and SO 2 solubility in ionic liquids. Key findings reveal that AI‐driven models improve predictive accuracy and real‐time monitoring, optimizing desulfurization processes, enhancing air quality, and supporting environmental sustainability. The study highlights the importance of hybrid AI models, improved data collection, and energy‐efficient practices to overcome field limitations. It underscores AI's transformative role in mitigating air pollution, controlling SO 2 emissions, and supporting the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals.

Wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) plays a central role in global food and nutritional security, but its productivity is challenged by biotic and abiotic stresses. Its large, polyploid genome and extensive repetitive sequences complicate the identification of genetic variation and the dissection of complex agronomic traits. This review examines emerging genomic resources and the complementary contributions of transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics and epigenomics to wheat improvement. High-throughput genotyping platforms, including SNP arrays, genotyping-by-sequencing and DArTseq, facilitate genetic diversity analysis and the identification of genomic regions associated with agronomic traits. Pan-genome approaches extend analyses beyond a single reference assembly by capturing structural, copy-number and presence–absence variation. Functional omics studies provide information on transcriptional regulation, protein responses, metabolite accumulation and chromatin-associated mechanisms involved in development and stress adaptation. The review also considers the use of artificial intelligence and machine learning for integrating complex datasets, predicting yield-related traits, automating phenotypic assessment and supporting genomic selection. Examples from wheat demonstrate the potential value of combining molecular information with computational approaches, although the reliability of predictions depends on data quality, representation and appropriate validation. Together, these advances provide complementary tools for identifying candidate genes and interpreting genotype–phenotype relationships. Their integration with reliable phenotypic information and established breeding practices may support more efficient wheat improvement while acknowledging the technical and biological challenges of translating molecular findings into breeding outcomes.
topics: Wheat and Barley Genetics and Pathology
