This study aims to examine and analyze human resource management (HRM) in addressing employee retention at Attafakur Orphanage Foundation in Jember. As a non-profit organization operating in the social sector, the foundation faces challenges in retaining potential employees due to limited financial resources compared to business organizations. Therefore, appropriate human resource management strategies are needed to improve organizational performance, maintain operational stability, and provide optimal services to children under the foundation’s care. This study employs a descriptive qualitative approach. The researcher served as the primary research instrument and an active participant in obtaining in-depth information. Primary data were collected through unstructured interviews with key informants, including the foundation’s chairperson, administrators, and the person in charge of the orphanage. Data were analyzed qualitatively through the stages of data collection, data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. Data validity was examined using triangulation techniques. The findings, based on Malayu S.P. Hasibuan’s theory, indicate that the foundation has implemented basic HRM functions, including planning, recruitment, development, motivation, compensation, and maintenance of working relationships, although in a relatively simple manner. Based on Mathis and Jackson’s theory, employee retention is primarily influenced by intrinsic motivation, including religious values, dedication, and inner satisfaction. In addition, participative leadership, a religious organizational culture, strong family-like relationships, and non-financial rewards contribute to employee retention. Meanwhile, the main obstacles to retention include limited financial compensation, high workloads, unstructured training programs, and external employment opportunities offering higher incomes

This Industrial Training report aims to analyze the performance of post insulators on lightning arresters (LA) and to understand their maintenance procedures at the 150 kV Cilegon Baru Substation, PT. PLN (Persero) ULTG Cilegon. The lightning arrester acts as a vital protective device to safeguard power system equipment against voltage surges caused by lightning or switching operations by diverting surge currents to the ground. The post insulator functions mechanically and electrically to support and isolate high-voltage components from the ground. The methodology involves field observation, maintenance participation, and data analysis of insulation resistance testing. The insulation resistance test results for the post insulator on phases R, S, and T were 10.6 MΩ, 2640 MΩ, and 10.2 MΩ, respectively. All measured values comply with the minimum standard requirement of 1 MΩ/kV, indicating that the equipment is in good and safe operational condition. Furthermore, maintenance procedures strictly adhere to Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) standards and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP).
topics: High voltage insulation and dielectric phenomena

documents.abstract: The article addresses the problem of teaching Russian grammar to adult international specialists in a non-language environment. The focus is on finding effective methods of teaching Russian as a Foreign Language (RFL) to Indian learners, when the traditional deductive approach, based on ready-made grammatical tables and reproductive exercises, fails to ensure meaningful comprehension of the material and speech production.The main problem tackled in the study is the contradiction between the need for rapid and conscious grammar acquisition by adult learners and the ineffectiveness of traditional forms of presenting material, which often lead to cognitive overload and superficial memorization.The aim of the research is to substantiate and describe an original teaching methodology grounded in the principles of andragogy. The methodology is based on the integration of problem-based learning, the cognitive approach, and the cooperative learning technology.The results of implementing this methodology in a group of 60 Indian specialists demonstrated its high effectiveness: 85% of learners completed the final test with “good” and “excellent” grades. The article concludes that the shift from the reproductive consumption of ready-made knowledge to its active construction enhances adult learners’ cognitive engagement, reduces anxiety, and fosters sustainable grammar skills.

This chapter analyses anticipatory governance as a public policy approach to strengthen state capacity in addressing emerging risks under conditions of high uncertainty. Drawing on a theoretical, comparative, and applied review, it examines how strategic foresight can be systematically integrated into the policy cycle, including formulation, implementation, and evaluation. The analysis identifies institutional mechanisms aimed at reducing systemic vulnerabilities in key domains such as public health, cybersecurity, energy transition, and artificial intelligence. It argues that effective anticipation depends less on precise forecasting and more on adaptive decision-making architectures, inter-institutional coordination, and continuous learning processes. The chapter also compares international experiences from Finland, Singapore, the United Kingdom, and the United States to extract lessons on analytical capacity, political leadership, regulatory quality, and democratic legitimacy.

BackgroundOccupational Health Check-ups (OHCs) have evolved from identifying work-related health risks to supporting sustainable employability through individualized lifestyle advice, but translating multidimensional demographic, occupational, and health characteristics into effective, personalized recommendations remains complex and lacks validated decision-support methods.ObjectiveAims of this study are to: 1) develop a Machine Learning Decision Support Tool (ML-DST) based on workers' demographic, occupational, and health characteristics to support personalized advice about lifestyle changes to improve sustainable employability, and 2) evaluate performance of the ML-DST.MethodsReal-world OHC data from a population-based cohort (2010-2020) were used to develop ML-DST models providing lifestyle advice (physical activity, smoking, alcohol, nutrition, relaxation, or no change) to improve workability and vitality. Paired baseline and 1-4-year follow-up data were used to train and evaluate 12 models. Per model, three rule-based algorithms were applied. Performance was considered useful when both True Positive Rate (TPR) and macroF1 score were ≥0.7. The best performing algorithm is proposed per model for inclusion in the final ML-DST.ResultsOf 20,440 individual OHCs, 3412 paired sets were included. Best TPRs ranged from 0.51 to 0.71. One model achieved TPR and macroF1 scores ≥0.7, supporting nutritional behavior change to improve vitality; however, its profiles were not conceptually meaningful. The other 11 models did not achieve useful quantitative performance.ConclusionTraining algorithms for an ML-DST to support advice about lifestyle changes to improve long-term sustainable employability using data from regular Occupational Health Check-ups did not lead to useful model performance for improving workability and vitality.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: As technology enables increasingly large, complex, and distributed team structures, new methods are needed to assess coordination in action teams. Recurrence Quantification Analysis (RQA) offers a powerful tool for capturing team coordination dynamics, yet its application to these modern teams remains methodologically underdeveloped. This paper identified and examined four characteristics of large action teams that contribute to analytical challenges when using RQA. We presented a systematic framework of Pre-Analytical Treatments, which are data preprocessing methods that can make RQA more computationally feasible while preserving meaningful team-level patterns. We then empirically evaluated three specific Pre-Analytical Treatments that either preserved temporal structure (Time Series) or controlled for periods of silence (Sequential, Dead-air Randomized). Using communication data from a 14-person expert team, we applied each treatment and examined their effects on RQA metrics and correlations with team trust, cohesion, and workload measures. Results demonstrated that these preprocessing decisions significantly affect RQA output relationships with team-level outcomes. Rather than advocating for a single approach, this study provides researchers with an empirically-grounded framework of methodological trade-offs to consider when applying RQA to large teams, offering both theoretical clarity about the impact of preprocessing decisions and practical guidance for selecting appropriate treatments based on research objectives.

This scoping review aims to systematically map the existing literature on the applications of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in depression care. It will explore how GenAI technologies, particularly large language models (LLMs) and AI-powered conversational agents, are being utilized across different stages of depression care, including screening, assessment, diagnosis, treatment, psychological support, and ongoing monitoring. The review will examine the characteristics of current applications, their reported effectiveness, feasibility, acceptability, and safety, as well as ethical considerations related to privacy, bias, reliability, and clinical accountability. By identifying emerging trends, evidence gaps, and methodological limitations, this review seeks to provide a comprehensive overview of the current research landscape and inform future research, clinical practice, and the responsible integration of GenAI into depression care.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: ABSTRACT Extant research has reported mixed evidence regarding the effectiveness of artificial intelligence (AI) recommendations in promoting green products, leaving it unclear under which conditions such recommendations are more (or less) effective. Drawing on Self‐Determination Theory (SDT), this research addresses this ambiguity by proposing a congruence effect between AI recommendation sources (substitute versus augmented AI) and green product attribute framing (utility‐based versus sustainability‐based). Using four scenario‐based online experiments (total N = 1114)—including one product choice task, one preference evaluation, and two studies measuring purchase intention and willingness to pay—this research demonstrates that substitute (augmented) AI recommendations are more effective for utility‐framed (sustainability‐framed) green products. Furthermore, consumers' sense of control mediates this congruence effect, and providing attribute‐based post hoc explanations eliminates the disadvantage of substitute AI under sustainability framing by shifting consumer responses toward sustainability‐framed green products. These findings advance understanding of human–AI interaction in green consumption and offer actionable insights for businesses seeking to leverage AI recommenders to increase the market share of green products.

Artificial intelligence (AI) tools, particularly large language models (LLMs), have rapidly integrated into surgical and biomedical research, prompting fundamental questions about their appropriate role. This review presents a stage-specific framework mapping each phase of the surgical research workflow (literature review, data analysis, manuscript preparation, and research synthesis) to the role AI plays, the benefits it provides, the failure modes it introduces, and the oversight it requires. Artificial intelligence-powered query systems are designed to speed literature synthesis across thousands of publications. In data analysis, LLMs paired with statistical environments can perform regression modeling and generate auditable code, while specialized architectures support automated image segmentation and histopathology analysis. Each stage's benefits, however, are matched by characteristic failure modes: LLMs are prone to error and hallucination, reproducibility is threatened by model versioning and run-to-run variability, fabricated citations and paper-mill submissions endanger the integrity of the literature, and over-reliance risks eroding trainee competencies in critical appraisal and biostatistical reasoning. Because these failure modes are stage-specific, governance must be stage-specific as well: the framework pairs each risk with a matched oversight mechanism, and these mechanisms translate into practical implementation recommendations for surgical departments, residency programs, research groups, and journals. The integration of AI into surgical scholarship should be viewed as augmentation rather than replacement, supported by standardized disclosure frameworks, AI literacy in graduate medical education, and institutional governance structures that preserve the integrity of surgical research.

documents.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies is transforming scholarly communication and knowledge-sharing practices in academic libraries worldwide. However, academic libraries in Nigeria and other African contexts continue to experience challenges related to limited visibility of research outputs, fragmented dissemination systems, uneven institutional repository development, information overload, and restricted access to scholarly resources. This paper presents a conceptual and analytical review of the strategic role of AI in strengthening scholarly communication and knowledge-sharing practices in African academic libraries. Drawing on recent scholarly literature, policy documents, and conceptual perspectives on digital transformation, the study examines the application of emerging AI technologies, including machine learning, natural language processing, recommender systems, and research analytics tools, in enhancing knowledge organisation, research discovery, open access integration, repository visibility, collaboration, and research evaluation. The paper further analyses contextual barriers affecting AI adoption, including inadequate digital infrastructure, funding limitations, professional capacity gaps, algorithmic bias, data privacy concerns, and weak institutional policy frameworks. Based on these analyses, the paper proposes a context-sensitive AI adoption framework that integrates technological readiness, institutional capacity, ethical governance, and policy support as essential dimensions for sustainable scholarly communication transformation. The paper concludes that strategic investment in digital infrastructure, librarian capacity development, inclusive data governance, and coordinated institutional policies is critical for ensuring that AI contributes to equitable, accessible, and sustainable knowledge-sharing ecosystems in African academic environments.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the way we discover anticancer drugs. It tackles the problems of traditional methods, such as prolonged timelines for drug development, higher costs, and substantial inter-patient heterogeneity. This review explains how AI is applied throughout the cancer drug pipeline. This includes target identification, virtual screening of compounds, molecular docking, and predicting pharmacokinetics. We explore how machine learning models speed up hit-to-lead optimization, improve clinical trial design by stratifying patients, and allow for real-time toxicity monitoring. A key focus is on integrating AI with multi-omics data, including proteomics, genomics, transcriptomics, and metabolomics, to support precision oncology and personalized treatments. We address important validation challenges, like model interpretability, data quality, and regulatory issues that must be solved before AI can be widely used in clinics. By summarizing current evidence and targeting research gaps, this review offers a clear view of how AI is enhancing the discovery, personalization, and validation of anticancer treatments.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Abstract Anaerobic digestion (AD) is a significant biological process that transforms organic waste into renewable biogas and nutrient-dense digestate. This can be returned as fertilizer, which promotes waste management and renewable energy production. However, typical monitoring relies on offline laboratory measurements of critical factors, including volatile fatty acids (VFAs) and chemical oxygen demand (COD), leading to reactive process management, instability, high costs, and suboptimal methane yields. Many anaerobic digestion plants operate based on experience rather than precise control strategies, making them highly vulnerable to acidification and spoilage due to fluctuations in pH, temperature, and organic loading rate. This overview investigates how artificial intelligence (AI), specifically machine learning (ML)-driven soft sensors and digital twins, infer difficult-to-measure variables from existing online sensors, enabling early instability detection and yield optimization. Key technical contributions include the unification of classical ML models (e.g., support vector machine (SVM), random forest) with deep learning for VFA prediction; hybrid physics-ML methods that use an AD model (ADM); and implementation of digital twins that achieve high accuracy (R2 > 0.94 for CH4 and pH). Current shortcomings include limited poor model portability, lack of AI interpretability, data quality issues, and low adoption of federated/reinforcement learning for autonomous control.
Decision-making is one of the most fundamental activities in many human, organizational,scientific, and societal contexts [...]
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: BackgroundThe use of artificial intelligence (AI) in workplace disability contexts is expanding, raising important ethical concerns. Existing frameworks, such as the OECD Framework for the Classification of AI Systems, provide structure for understanding AI applications but lack an explicit focus on ethics in relation to disability.ObjectiveThis systematic review examines ethical issues arising from the use of AI for employees with disabilities and aims to interpret the OECD framework through an explicit ethics lens.MethodsWe conducted a systematic review of 23 peer-reviewed studies identified through PRISMA-guided searches. Using the OECD AI framework as a foundation, we developed an extended multidimensional framework consisting of five interconnected domains: (1) Context, (2) People, (3) Data & Input, (4) AI Model, and (5) Task & Output and analyzed through the lens of ethics.ResultsFour recurring ethical concerns were identified: (1) automation bias, (2) data privacy and informed consent, (3) discrimination and inequitable access to opportunities, and (4) AI governance gaps. Ethical risks were found to be context-dependent, disproportionately affecting disabled workers, and exacerbated by biased or incomplete data and opaque AI models.ConclusionsThis review provides a structured synthesis of current evidence and highlights the need for responsible and inclusive AI practices. We propose key directions for research and practice, including algorithmic audits, inclusive testing, transparent data practices, interdisciplinary oversight, and worker-centered governance. Integrating ethics throughout a multidimensional framework offers a roadmap for advancing equitable AI in workplace disability contexts.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: We ask what artificial intelligence (AI) is actually doing to macroeconomic growth in the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, and by what route. Three channels are considered: efficiency gains, wider financial inclusion, and lower transaction costs. The paper also treats the “Commercial Banking Applications” platform, hereafter CBAs, as a mediating channel, based on the argument that innovation only reaches the real economy when some concrete piece of infrastructure carries it there. The design is mixed and descriptive–analytical. On the quantitative side, a questionnaire was administered to 403 respondents drawn from employees and experts across Jordan’s banking and financial environment. On the qualitative side, we conducted semi-structured interviews with a purposive sample of 12 experts and senior officials. Among these, the Central Bank, the Securities Commission, and the Association of Banks were represented, along with founders of financial technology start-ups. Structural and path relationships were estimated in AMOS, supported by multiple regression. AI has a statistically significant positive effect on growth overall. The total effect is 0.829 at a significance level of 0.000, and the model accounts for 65.9% of the variance in economic growth. CBAs carry a substantial share of that. Its indirect effect is 0.341, or 34.1%, delivered mainly by cutting the time and effort a transaction takes and by holding together an otherwise fragmented set of financial connections, with liquidity rising as a result. The main recommendation of this article follows from this: invest in comprehensive financial connectivity. Financial connectivity and integration proved to be the factor most closely linked with growth, which makes it necessary to invest in the development of flexible technological channels for the growth of digital systems and to ensure the technical simplicity of interactions between Commercial Banking Applications, start-ups, and government agencies.

Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, is increasingly embedded in knowledge work, creative work, customer service, product development, human resource management, and organizational decision systems. Although research shows that AI can raise productivity, support creative output, accelerate searching, and reorganize innovation work, the evidence remains fragmented across innovation management, organizational behavior, information systems, human resource management, economics, human–computer interaction, and behavioral sciences. This framework-based review synthesizes high-quality English-language journal articles on AI, human–AI collaboration, employee creativity, innovative work behavior, algorithmic management, and innovation management. Building on established models of individual innovation, it develops a worker-centered framework linking four innovation stages with three higher-order AI functions: task execution, knowledge support, and organizational governance. The evidence is strongest for searching, idea generation, creativity, and short-term task performance, and remains limited for idea promotion, implementation, diffusion, and realized innovation outcomes. The synthesis identifies three central tensions: performance equalization versus capability differentiation, short-term quality versus long-term capability development, and individual improvement versus collective homogenization. AI can enhance innovation-related work through cognitive expansion, search acceleration, productivity release, recombination, feedback, and learning, but it can also reduce output diversity, weaken expertise development, intensify work, increase dependence, and shift managerial control over creative labor. The review positions AI as both a cognitive resource and an innovation-governance mechanism and outlines directions for future research on mechanisms, heterogeneity, novelty, capability accumulation, and responsible governance.

Measurement and regular monitoring of key water quality parameters, either in natural water bodies or in an engineered wastewater treatment plant (WWTP), are essential for assessing the overall system performance or identifying the root causes of water quality degradation. Advances in machine learning (ML) algorithms, remote sensing, and soft sensors have been transformative for water quality management programs. Satellite imagery and calibrated spectral indices can be used for long-term water quality monitoring or for a machine-learning-based water quality index. Data-driven ML models trained on historical data on influent characteristics, operating parameters, and labeled performance in municipal WWTPs can predict treatment efficiency and effluent quality. This chapter starts with an introduction to various ML model architectures, highlighting the stages in the model development exercise. The application of ML models in wastewater treatment and water quality prediction is discussed in subsequent sections. Finally, challenges and future perspectives in this domain are addressed.
